note: AUDIT-021 drove this to zero and it is now a HARD GATE at 0: check:no-random-metrics fails on the first object property whose value comes from Math.random(), i.e. a measurement someone made up. Keyed by file and property name so line moves do not churn it. Do not add entries - the guard exists because a random metric changes on every request, which is exactly what real telemetry does, so refreshing appears to confirm it. See scripts/check-no-random-metrics.mjs, AUDIT-020 and AUDIT-021. Known blind spots, stated so a pass is never read as proof: the rule is line-anchored, so a single-line object literal escapes it; it watches a PROPERTY, so a random value passed positionally into a query does not trip it (CR-017's seeder-in-disguise was one); and a value invented as a plain literal is check:fabricated's and check:no-static-posture's territory, not this one.
